question: What do we mean by body alignment in nursing care?

options.A: How skeletal and muscular systems maintain balance against gravity
options.B: The physical distance a patient can walk without resting
options.C: A measurement of total muscle mass in the lower limbs
options.D: The specific angle at which a hospital bed is elevated

explanation: Think of body alignment as how your bones and muscles work together like a team to keep you upright and balanced against gravity, preventing strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is proper body support so important for patients who spend all day in bed?

options.A: It prevents skin breakdown and joint contractures
options.B: It completely cures chronic bone infections
options.C: It increases the patient's daily calorie intake
options.D: It eliminates the need for daily vital signs

explanation: Great job! Proper support spreads out the patient's weight evenly, keeping pressure sores away and stopping joints from freezing up in stiff positions. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Where is the body's center of gravity usually located when standing normally?

options.B: In the center of the pelvis
options.C: At the top of the skull

explanation: When standing straight, our center of balance or gravity is right around our pelvic area. Knowing this helps us understand how our bodies stay stable! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: What happens when someone's line of gravity moves outside their base of support?

options.D: The person loses balance and falls

explanation: Spot on! If your center of balance wanders outside your footing, gravity takes over and down you go. That's why wide stances keep us steady. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does poor, slumped posture affect a patient's breathing?

options.A: It stops the movement of the diaphragm completely
options.B: It increases the total volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: It causes rapid overinflation of the chest cavity
options.D: It restricts lung expansion and reduces oxygen intake

explanation: Slumping scrunches up the chest cavity, leaving the lungs with very little room to stretch out and take in a deep, refreshing breath. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why can slouching lead to tummy troubles like heartburn or constipation?

options.B: It makes the liver swell in size
options.C: It speeds up intestinal transit too much
options.D: It stops the production of stomach acid

explanation: When you slouch, your upper body squeezes your tummy and intestines like a pinched pipe, which makes digestion a bit uncomfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which food nutrients are most important for keeping bones strong and posture upright?
explanation: Calcium and vitamin D are the ultimate dynamic duo for bone health! They build strong bones and help prevent weakness or spinal curving. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: A patient with severe tummy pain walks into the clinic bent forward. What is causing this posture?
explanation: This is called 'guarding.' It's a natural, protective reflex where the body curls inward to shield a painful spot from touch or stretch. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: What do we call the medical condition where the upper back curves outward into a hunchback shape?
explanation: Kyphosis is the term for an exaggerated rounding of the upper back. You'll often spot this in elderly patients during routine assessments! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: What causes foot drop in bedridden patients who don't get proper nursing support?

options.A: Wearing compression stockings that are too tight
options.B: Walking too much on hard hospital floors without shoes
options.C: Drinking too little water during daytime shifts
options.D: Leaving the feet unsupported in plantar flexion for too long

explanation: When toes point downward unsupported for days, the calf muscles and Achilles tendon tighten up permanently. Simple foot supports easily prevent this! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h5)

question: When checking a patient's standing posture from behind, what is the first thing a nurse should look for?

options.A: Symmetry of the shoulders and hips
options.B: The strength of the hand grip
options.C: The speed of the patient's heart rate
options.D: The exact color of the patient's eyes

explanation: By checking if both shoulders and hips line up evenly, you can quickly spot early signs of spinal curves like scoliosis. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is watching a patient walk (a gait assessment) so important for nurses?

options.A: It reveals how well the patient balances while moving and indicates fall risk
options.B: It shows whether the patient is digesting food properly
options.C: It measures the exact lung capacity of the patient
options.D: It tests the cranial nerves inside the brain

explanation: Watching how someone walks tells you a lot about their balance and muscle strength, helping you keep them safe from accidental falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the safest way to bend down and pick up a heavy item off the floor?

options.A: Bend at your knees and hips while keeping your back straight
options.B: Twist your upper body sideways as you reach down
options.C: Arch your back backward before lifting upward
options.D: Bend forward only at your waist with stiff knees

explanation: Always let your strong leg muscles do the heavy lifting instead of your back! Keeping your back straight protects your spine. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: You need to help turn a heavy patient in bed. Which movement should you avoid to protect your back?

options.A: Adjusting the bed to a comfortable working height
options.B: Twisting your waist while pulling the patient toward you
options.C: Widening your stance to create a stable base of support
options.D: Asking a colleague to help you slide the patient

explanation: Never twist your back while lifting or pulling! Always pivot with your feet instead to save your spinal discs from injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which nursing device is used to keep a patient's hips from rolling outward during bed rest?
explanation: A trochanter roll tucked snugly beside the thigh keeps the hip joint nice and neutral, stopping the leg from rolling outward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why do nurses use slide sheets when moving a patient from a bed to a stretcher?

options.A: They replace the need for any nurses to assist
options.B: They act as a heating pad to warm up the patient
options.C: They automatically record the patient's weight
options.D: They reduce friction and shearing forces on the patient's skin

explanation: Slide sheets are a nurse's best friend! They make patients glide smoothly, protecting fragile skin from friction and saving your back from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h8)
